title: For you — the timeline ranked the way X ranks its home timeline

tasks.title: Rank For you and the conversation

acs.text: WHEN the viewer opens the second tab (labelled "For you", API `tab=everyone`) THE SYSTEM SHALL rank every post from the last 14 days (at most 500) for that viewer with X's heavy-ranker sum, score = Σ weight(a) × P(a), using X's published weights (fav 0.5, repost 1.0, reply 13.5, reply engaged by author 75, negative feedback −74, report −369) and a quote weight of 12.5; P(a) is the post's own engagement per follower of its author, smoothed toward a prior, and lifted by the viewer's own recent engagement with that author. The score halves every 24 hours from the post's latest boost (posted, reposted or quoted). A post from outside the viewer's network is × 0.75 (X's OONTweetScalingScorer) unless a profile the viewer follows reposted it, in which case it says who.
scenarios: AC-001 engagement and the network decide the order

acs.text: THE SYSTEM SHALL spread authors out: after scoring, each further post by the same author in the ranking is × 0.5, down to × 0.25 (X's author-diversity rescoring). Pages are 20 with a cursor that keeps the ranking's time, so "Show more" never repeats a post.
scenarios: AC-002 one author does not fill the page

acs.text: WHEN a post's page is read THE SYSTEM SHALL order its replies: the post's author's own first, then replies from profiles the viewer follows, then the rest, oldest first within each.
scenarios: AC-003 the conversation puts the author first

acs.text: The ranking SHALL be one pure module (services/ranking.ts) whose constants name their source (X's code or our choice), tested on its own.
scenarios: AC-004 the scoring is X's sum
